title: Incident Review: API Gateway 5xx Surge During Autoscaler Warmup (2026-03-10, us-east-1)
author: Marco Ruiz
content:
## Summary
On 2026-03-10 between 18:05–19:40 UTC, we experienced a sustained increase in 5xx responses for a subset of production traffic in us-east-1, primarily affecting ClearMind AI (dedicated tenant). The incident manifested as API gateway queue buildup (accept queue), elevated hedged retries, and serving-runtime watchdog-triggered restarts (crashloop-like behavior), resulting in 502/503/504 responses.

A temporary per-tenant rate limit and a small prewarm increase stabilized the system within ~25 minutes; however, elevated 5xx for the affected tenant persisted intermittently until retries were capped and runtime soft-shedding was deployed.

## Customer impact
- Customer: ClearMind AI (dedicated)
- Impacted routes: /v1/chat (streaming) and embedding endpoints
- Peak error rate: ~35% (per tenant) on the affected routes during the peak window
- Other tenants: us-east-1 experienced increased tail latency; no sustained platform-wide 5xx beyond short transients

## What happened (technical)
The event was an amplification loop:
1) A burst of concurrent streaming chat sessions + high-rate embedding uploads increased queueing pressure at the API gateway.
2) Autoscaler scale-ups were slower than expected during a warmup window, resulting in fewer ready serving-runtime workers than demand required.
3) API gateway hedged retries escalated when accept_queue exceeded the retry trigger threshold; this increased request fanout to already overloaded runtimes.
4) Serving-runtime hit long GPU stall watchdog thresholds (observed nvml timeout symptoms on a subset of nodes) and restarted processes. These restarts further reduced capacity and increased 5xx.

Important update vs. initial hypothesis:
- Early investigation attributed the slow scale-up primarily to cloud quota API 429s. Deeper review (cloud events + autoscaler controller metrics) showed that quota throttling contributed, but the larger driver was a warm pool configuration regression introduced on 2026-03-08 that reduced effective prewarm and made scale steps more bursty. This misconfiguration increased cold starts and extended the time-to-ready during a demand spike.

## Timeline (UTC)
- 18:05: Initial warning signs. api-gateway accept queue rises rapidly for /v1/chat.
- 18:06–18:10: Autoscaler requests capacity; time-to-ready degrades. Some cloud instance create calls return 429, but controller also shows repeated warm-pool depletion.
- 18:08–18:20: serving-runtime watchdog evictions and restarts begin on several workers. Gateway 502/503 increases; retries accelerate.
- 18:22: Emergency per-tenant rate limit applied for ClearMind AI (embed/chat). Queue starts to drain.
- 18:35: Rolling restart of the most affected runtime instances (GPU/NVML state) begins; core dumps gathered.
- 19:05: Customer notified; client-side backoff enabled.
- 19:40: Primary incident window ends; tenant error rate returns near baseline with mitigations in place.
- 2026-03-12: Runtime hotfix merged (soft-shed before watchdog restart) in PR #4821.
- 2026-03-14: Hotfix canary deployed in us-east-1; no regressions detected.
- 2026-03-15: Hotfix fully rolled out; gateway retry cap and backpressure adjustments enabled.

## Signals and evidence
### Representative logs
- 2026-03-10T18:05:12Z apigw[edge-01] WARN accept_queue_size=620 route=/v1/chat status=queueing
- 2026-03-10T18:07:01Z autoscaler[controller] INFO scale_event=requested=18 provisioned=6 reason=warm_pool_depleted wait=120s
- 2026-03-10T18:08:45Z runtime[worker-3] ERROR watchdog: gpu_stall=12.8s -> evicting task id=xx34; initiating process-restart
- 2026-03-10T18:09:03Z apigw[edge-01] ERROR upstream_response=502 backend=serving-runtime-3 trace=trace-9f2a
- 2026-03-10T18:15:22Z kvcache[embed-shard] WARN eviction_lag=340ms prefetch_lock=true

### Key observations
- api-gateway hedged retries increased ~8x once accept_queue exceeded ~500.
- Serving-runtime restarts were clustered on a subset of GPU hosts with intermittent nvml timeout warnings; restarts reduced effective capacity and increased retry-induced load.
- NVMe iowait spikes correlated with background snapshotting of an embedding shard, which increased prefetch latency and contributed to backlog.

## Root cause
Primary cause:
- Warm pool configuration regression reduced effective prewarm capacity and increased time-to-ready under bursty demand, allowing gateway queues to build.

Contributing factors:
- API gateway hedged retry policy amplified load when accept_queue exceeded the retry threshold (fanout under stress).
- Serving-runtime watchdog behavior prioritized process restart after GPU stall thresholds, which under heavy load reduced capacity further instead of shedding gracefully.
- Background NVMe-intensive snapshotting increased prefetch latency during the same window.
- Cloud provider throttling (429) during instance creation was present but not the sole or dominant driver.

## Mitigation during the incident
Immediate actions (during 18:20–19:40 UTC):
1) Applied emergency per-tenant rate limit for ClearMind AI on embed/chat routes.
2) Restarted affected runtime instances to clear GPU/NVML state and collected diagnostics.
3) Increased prewarm pool in us-east-1 to reduce cold starts.
4) Recommended customer-side backoff and reduced concurrency profile.

Result:
- Reduced 5xx from ~35% to <2% for the impacted tenant within ~25 minutes; remaining intermittent errors were addressed by follow-up deployments.

## Permanent fixes (implemented)
1) Serving-runtime soft-shed path added to return 429/503 gracefully before watchdog restart under sustained GPU stalls (PR #4821). Rolled out fully by 2026-03-15.
2) API gateway retry policy updated:
   - Added a hard cap on hedged retries under high accept_queue.
   - Disabled hedging for streaming routes when upstream saturation is detected.
3) Autoscaler warm pool configuration guarded:
   - Added config validation + alerting for effective prewarm dropping below baseline.
   - Reduced aggressive scale step sizing to avoid bursty cold starts.
4) Snapshot scheduling:
   - Moved embedding shard snapshotting out of known peak windows for dedicated tenants.

## What went well
- On-call identified accept_queue + retry amplification quickly and reduced load with a targeted tenant rate limit.
- Cross-team collaboration (SRE + runtime + autoscaler) enabled a fast mitigation and a production-safe runtime fix.

## What didn’t go well
- Initial attribution over-weighted cloud quota throttling; warm pool regression detection was delayed due to insufficient guardrails/alerts.
- Gateway retry behavior was insufficiently bounded under saturation, increasing blast radius to runtimes.
- Runtime watchdog policy optimized for recovery but not for stability under sustained overload.

## Action items (current status as of 2026-03-21)
- SRE (Marco Ruiz): Add alert for accept_queue + hedged_retry_rate coupling (DONE).
- Runtime (Jillian Kim): Complete NVML timeout deep dive and document recommended driver/firmware baselines (IN PROGRESS; target 2026-04-05).
- Autoscaler (Priya Desai): Add backpressure input from api-gateway accept_queue to scale logic to prevent retry amplification feedback loops (IN PROGRESS; target 2026-04-12).
- Platform (Tom Nguyen): Add route-level automatic graceful-shed behavior at gateway when accept_queue exceeds threshold, returning 429 with Retry-After for eligible clients (IN PROGRESS; target 2026-04-19).

## Reproduction notes (staging)
A smaller-scale reproduction was achieved in staging by:
1) Running continuous embedding upload (~5000 small vectors/min) plus ~250 concurrent short chat streaming sessions for ~20 minutes.
2) Reducing warm pool growth / limiting warm capacity to simulate slow time-to-ready.
3) Observing accept_queue depth, retry rates, runtime watchdog events, and storage iowait during snapshotting.

## References
- Primary support ticket: SUP-175001
- Related incidents/issues: SUP-246750, SUP-68410
- Runtime hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/ephemeral-scaler-warmup-5xx

## Appendix: Metrics to monitor going forward
- api-gateway: accept_queue_size, hedged_retry_rate, upstream_5xx_rate by route (especially streaming)
- autoscaler: time_to_ready_p50/p95, warm_pool_effective_capacity, scale_step_size
- serving-runtime: watchdog_evictions, restart_rate, GPU stall duration distributions
- storage: NVMe iowait, snapshot duration, prefetch latency
